purpose: Teach: 終焉/連立/決戦/火力/耕/媒介/シリア/精進

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、論文、ローマ帝国の終焉、よく、まとめましたね、視点が、独創的でした。
lines.en: Ren, your paper on the fall of the Roman Empire was really well put together. Your perspective was genuinely original.
lines.style: Warm, measured encouragement. Steady eye contact. A slight pause before delivering the compliment—not hesitation, but giving weight to the praise. Genuinely pleased.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。戦後、連立政権の歴史、各国比較で、論じました。
lines.en: Yes. I approached it through post-war coalition governments across different countries.
lines.style: Respectful but engaged. Modest without self-deprecation. Slight upward lift at the start—acknowledging the teacher's point and moving forward with his own thinking. Natural, conversational pace.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 冷戦の決戦地、各国に、影響を、与えていますね、今も、痕跡が、残ります。
lines.en: The Cold War's turning points affected so many countries differently. The traces are still visible today.
lines.style: Thoughtful, almost musing. Slower pace. Speaking as though the teacher is thinking aloud alongside him, not lecturing. Gently exploratory tone.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。火力発電が、近代産業を、支えた基盤、論じました、第二章で。
lines.en: Yes. I argued in my second chapter that thermal power generation was actually the foundation that supported modern industry through that period.
lines.style: Careful, precise delivery. Not defensive, but exact—wanting to be understood clearly. Slight emphasis on 'second chapter' to ground his point. Earnest without being stiff.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 戦時の食糧難、田を耕す人々の絆、深く、論じていますね、感動的でした。
lines.en: The food shortages during the war, and the bonds between people farming the land—you wrote about that quite deeply. It was really moving.
lines.style: Warm recognition. Voice softens slightly on 'bonds' and 'moving.' Not gushing, but genuine emotion. A teacher noticing something true in the work beyond academic merit.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。病気の媒介、衛生概念の変遷、戦後の医療、変えました。
lines.en: Yes. I traced how disease vectors and changing concepts of hygiene actually transformed post-war medicine.
lines.style: Animated, a bit more engaged now. Pride in the work coming through, but controlled. Speaking with quiet confidence—this is something he knows. Not rushed, but more assured than before.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: シリアの古代文明、文化交流の交差点でしたね、論文の中でも、触れていますね。
lines.en: Ancient Syria as a cultural crossroads was fascinating too. I noticed you touched on that in the paper as well.
lines.style: Genuine interest. A slight tilt forward in the voice—noticing and appreciating a detail. Not overstating it, but showing she read carefully and recognized his reach.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。日々の精進、研究者として、心がけてまいります、ありがとうございました。
lines.en: Yes. I'll continue to work diligently as a researcher. Thank you very much.
lines.style: Respectful, sincere closing. Not rushed. A small breath before the gratitude—letting the moment land. Formal but warm, genuine deference without stiffness.
